clue.text: Don't forget about MP

parts.note: re is Latin-derived for 'concerning, about'
an MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A reminder not to overlook your parliamentary representative.
explanation.definitionFit: The imperative 'Don't forget' is a plain synonym of the command to keep something in mind.

clue.text: Regret bringing in Liberal government

indicators.note: bringing something in means taking it inside, so the regret word wraps around the single letter

parts.note: to rue is to regret
L is the standard abbreviation for Liberal

explanation.surface: Someone lamenting the arrival of a Liberal administration.
explanation.definitionFit: Rule is the exercise of authority over a country, which is a synonym for government.

clue.text: Play in match and be beaten

indicators.note: something beaten is knocked out of shape, so these letters are battered into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sports report about a team losing a game.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's tragedy about the Scottish king is an example of a play.

clue.text: Central square?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: politically in the centre, moderate

explanation.walkthrough: Read together the two words suggest a square in the middle of a town; separately they are two senses of one hyphenated phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes both moderate politics, avoiding extremes, and bland conventional taste, which is what 'square' means as slang.

clue.text: More in next race

indicators.note: 'in' tells us the answer sits inside the run of words that follows

parts.note: the letters run across the two words, inside them

explanation.surface: Further excitement promised for the following race at a meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: Extra means additional, so it works as a synonym for 'more'.

clue.text: Computer circuit to power

parts.note: a lap is one circuit of a track
taken as written
P is the symbol for power in physics

explanation.surface: Instructions for wiring an electronic circuit up to the mains.
explanation.definitionFit: A laptop is a portable personal machine, a kind of computer.

clue.text: Locates refurbished rooms very near…

indicators.note: refurbishing a thing remakes it, so these letters are reworked into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
quarters are lodgings or rooms

explanation.surface: An estate agent finds renovated rooms right next door.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes being in close proximity, so it means very near.

clue.text: …Partick, let out after this?

definitions.note: the answer completes the name Partick Thistle

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: 'out' suggests something put out of place, so the three letters before it are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Following on from the previous clue, someone being released by a Glasgow football club.
explanation.walkthrough: Partick Thistle is a Glasgow football club, so the answer is the word that follows 'Partick'. The scrambled word comes after 'this' in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Partick Thistle is the full name of the Scottish football club, so the answer is the missing half of that name.

clue.text: Large case of wine, fine mixture

parts.note: port is a fortified wine
F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils
an olio is a medley or miscellany

explanation.surface: A big box holding a blend of good wines.
explanation.definitionFit: A portfolio is a large flat carrying case for papers or drawings.

clue.text: Clear chance, virtually, I had

indicators.note: 'virtually' means almost, so the word is taken all but its final letter

parts.note: luck is chance, before trimming
I'd is the contraction of 'I had'

explanation.surface: A footballer recalling an open goal-scoring opportunity he nearly had.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucid means easy to understand, a synonym of clear.

clue.text: Bellman in tricorn we jostled

indicators.note: things jostled are pushed about, so these letters are pushed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A bell-ringer in a three-cornered hat being pushed about by a crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: The tricorn hat is part of the traditional costume of the official, which makes the surface picture apt.
explanation.definitionFit: A town crier rang a handbell before making public announcements, so he was known as a bellman.

clue.text: We must get harmful insect

parts.note: taken as written
evil means harmful or wicked

explanation.surface: A call to obtain some damaging bug, perhaps for an experiment.
explanation.definitionFit: A weevil is a small beetle, so it is a type of insect.

clue.text: Spill the beans, as children are inclined to do?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: reveal secrets or gossip indiscreetly

definitions.text: as children are inclined to do?
definitions.meaning: second meaning, taken literally: pupils telling stories about classmates once away from the classroom

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the second half reads the idiom literally, about children carrying stories home from class.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to give away confidential information, the same as spilling the beans.

clue.text: See 12
Assistant editor and writer contribute money

parts.note: a sub is a sub-editor, an assistant editor
a scribe is a writer

explanation.surface: Newspaper staff chipping in for a collection.
explanation.definitionFit: To subscribe is to pledge or pay a sum to a fund or cause, so it means contribute money.

clue.text: Genuine, following team of stars

indicators.note: 'following' places the first word after the next one in the answer

parts.note: a side is a team
real means genuine

explanation.surface: A sports fan praising an authentic squad of star players.
explanation.definitionFit: Sidereal is the astronomical adjective meaning relating to the stars.

clue.text: Iron clubs hidden by little girl in grass

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

indicators.note: something hidden by another is covered by it, so the second item wraps around the first

parts.note: Sue is a short girl's name
C is the abbreviation for clubs in cards

explanation.surface: A child has hidden golf clubs in the long grass.
explanation.definitionFit: Fescue is a genus of tufted grasses widely used for lawns, so it is a kind of grass.

clue.text: Infatuated with OT in finest edition

indicators.note: 'in' says the first item goes inside the word after it

parts.note: best means finest
OT, the Old Testament, taken as written
ed. is the abbreviation for edition

explanation.surface: A book lover smitten with a superb printing of the Old Testament.
explanation.definitionFit: Besotted means strongly infatuated, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Arrange to go round a US city

indicators.note: going round something means surrounding it, so one word wraps the letter

parts.note: to settle a matter is to arrange it
taken as written

explanation.surface: Planning a tour around an American city.
explanation.definitionFit: Seattle is the largest city in Washington state, in the United States.

clue.text: Crazy chef reportedly needing two ducks

indicators.note: 'reportedly' means as heard, so we take the sound of the word rather than its spelling

parts.note: a chef is a cook, said in the British way
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, which looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: A cook, so the story goes, demanding a pair of ducks for a dish.
explanation.walkthrough: In British speech the first syllable of the answer rhymes with 'book'. A duck in cricket is a score of zero, hence O.
explanation.definitionFit: Cuckoo is informal for mad or crazy, from the bird's repetitive call.

clue.text: Clever clogs on walk corrected about length

indicators.note: 'about' means surrounding, so the rearranged letters go around the single letter
something corrected is changed and put right, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
L is the abbreviation for length

explanation.surface: A smart alec on a stroll being put right about some distance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clever clogs' is British slang for a show-off who thinks they know best.
explanation.definitionFit: A know-all is someone who acts as if they know everything, which is what a clever clogs does.

clue.text: Famous lawyer and daughter quarrel at the back of carriage

indicators.note: 'at the back of' places the first pieces after the last one in the answer

parts.note: a clarence is a closed four-wheeled horse-drawn carriage
D is the abbreviation for daughter
a quarrel is a crossbow bolt, a kind of arrow

explanation.surface: A barrister and his daughter rowing in the back of a car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quarrel' wants to mean a row, but here it is the short heavy arrow fired from a crossbow.
explanation.definitionFit: Clarence Darrow was the celebrated American defence attorney of the Scopes trial, so he is a famous lawyer.

clue.text: Dump in Channel

definitions.meaning: first meaning: get rid of, abandon
second meaning: a dug trench for water

explanation.surface: Dumping waste in the English Channel.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for discarding something and a noun for a narrow drainage trench.

clue.text: Girl on river for a month in Israel?

parts.note: Ada is a girl's name
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A young woman spends a month on an Israeli river.
explanation.definitionFit: Adar is the twelfth month of the Hebrew calendar, used in Israel; the question mark marks it as an example.

clue.text: Reticent person in car going through the heart of Brittany

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: going through something passes inside it, so the vehicle sits within the kept letters
the heart of a word is its middle, so only its central letters are kept

parts.note: the two central letters of the eight-letter name
Rover is a British make of car

explanation.surface: A shy traveller driving through the middle of Brittany in France.
explanation.definitionFit: An introvert is a reserved, inward-looking person, so a reticent person.

clue.text: Last in tribe to capture an antelope

indicators.note: 'last in' points to the final letter of the following word only

parts.note: the final letter of the word
to land a fish or prize is to capture it

explanation.surface: The final hunter of a tribe setting out to catch an antelope.
explanation.definitionFit: The eland is a large African species, so it is an antelope.

clue.text: Finishes checking me and makes corrections

indicators.note: checking can mean holding back or restraining, so one word holds the other within it

parts.note: ends are finishes
taken as written

explanation.surface: An editor completes proofreading my work and fixes errors.
explanation.definitionFit: To emend is to edit a text to remove errors, so emends means makes corrections.

clue.text: Painter in card game right next to the Parisian

indicators.note: 'next to' places one piece directly beside another, so the pieces join side by side

parts.note: whist is a trick-taking card game
le is French for 'the'
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: An artist sitting at a card table beside a Frenchman.
explanation.walkthrough: The order is game, then the French word, then the letter it sits next to.
explanation.definitionFit: James McNeill Whistler was an American-born painter, famous for 'Whistler's Mother'.
